title: Geese Take Turns at the Front
core_idea: Geese flying in formation take turns leading against the wind; their rhythm suggests that resting and letting others carry the front is part of any shared journey.
text: Watch a flock of geese crossing an autumn sky, and you may notice the shape shifting. The bird at the front of the V works hardest against the wind. After a while, it drifts back, and another takes its place. No one leads forever. Perhaps there's something in that for us. Many of us believe we must always be the strong one, the one who carries everyone. But even geese know when to fall back into the slipstream and let others hold the front for a while. Resting is not failing the flock. It's part of how the whole journey becomes possible.
description: A calm reflection on geese taking turns at the front of the flock, and what that might teach us about rest.
